hypotheses.justification: The statement never uses `CharZero K`. `padicCompletionUnitsRepresentation p L K` only needs commutative-semiring instances and `[Fact p.Prime]` (Basic.lean, section GaloisAction). It follows from the other hypotheses. `algebraMap K L` is injective because `K` is a field and `L` is nontrivial. Mathlib's `RingHom.charZero_iff` (Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/CharZero.lean:57) says `Injective ϕ → (CharZero R ↔ CharZero S)`. So `(RingHom.charZero_iff (algebraMap K L).injective).mpr inferInstance` gives `CharZero K` from `[CharZero L]`. It also follows from `[Algebra ℚ_[p] K]` and Mathlib's `CharZero ℚ_[p]` instance. The proof only uses `CharZero K` through the private lemma `groupCohomology_res_padicCompletionUnits`, via `strictCohomologicalDimensionAt_galSeparableClosure_eq_two`. With `omit [CharZero K] in`, the proof becomes `haveI : CharZero K := (RingHom.charZero_iff (algebraMap K L).injective).mpr inferInstance; exact (groupCohomology_res_padicCompletionUnits p K L S).2`. No degenerate case arises, since `K` and `L` are fields. `[CharZero L]` can also be deleted on its own (next entry). Both can go at once, because each still follows from `ℚ_[p]` through `[Algebra ℚ_[p] K]` or `[Algebra ℚ_[p] L]`.

The statement never uses `CharZero L`. Neither `padicCompletionUnitsRepresentation p L K`, `Rep.of`, `Rep.res` nor `groupCohomology` requires it. It follows from the other hypotheses: `(RingHom.charZero_iff (algebraMap K L).injective).mp inferInstance` turns `[CharZero K]` into `CharZero L`. It also follows from `(RingHom.charZero_iff (algebraMap ℚ_[p] L).injective).mp inferInstance`, using Mathlib's `CharZero ℚ_[p]` instance (PadicNumbers.lean:568). After `omit [CharZero L] in`, the proof first runs `haveI : CharZero L := ...` and then applies `groupCohomology_res_padicCompletionUnits` unchanged. That lemma and the lemmas it calls (`classModuleAddEquiv`, local reciprocity) need `CharZero L` only as an instance argument, and the local instance supplies it.
